title: Mobile Repository Acquisition, App-Private Workspace, and Explicit Import/Export Implementation

preflight.note: Stamped by `repopact new` at WI061 closeout, as required by WI061 AC-5: WI061 decided (Decision 0056) that mobile repositories are app-private ordinary filesystem workspaces acquired via SAF import, archive import, or (Stage 2) embedded Git, and explicitly deferred all implementation to this follow-up. This item implements Stage 1 only (SAF/archive import into an app-private workspace, normal Workbench operation, explicit export/share-back); Stage 2 embedded Git is out of scope here.

acceptance_criteria.text: A production mobile workspace registry exists: an app-owned record of each acquired workspace (workspace id, display name, acquisition kind, source reference, created/imported time, last export/sync state, Git/non-Git) persisted in app-private storage, containing no credential material, and not acting as a new global governance authority (per Decision 0056).

select_repository (or a new typed mobile acquisition command set) on Android offers SAF-based acquisition: ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT_TREE for a directory, and ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT for a single archive, replacing the current unconditional `repository.mobile-selection-unavailable` error on a normal production build with a real acquisition flow. No broad storage permission (e.g. MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE) is added; the debug-only android_validation.rs path may be retired once production acquisition covers its purpose.

Safe recursive directory import from a picked SAF tree into the app-private workspace is implemented with bounded resource handling, a defined symlink policy, defined duplicate-name behavior, no path traversal or writes outside the allocated workspace root, cancellation, and partial-import cleanup, proven by adversarial tests (traversal attempt, symlink escape attempt, oversized/pathological tree).

Safe archive import (.zip or equivalent) into the app-private workspace is implemented with zip-slip/absolute-path/`..`-traversal rejection, symlink-escape protection, entry-count/expanded-byte/depth bounds against archive bombs, duplicate/case-conflicting path handling, and cleanup after failed extraction, proven by adversarial tests using deliberately malicious fixture archives.

DesktopService/RepositorySession open and operate on an app-private workspace produced by AC-3 or AC-4 exactly as they do on desktop -- normal Workbench IA, real Rust-backed reads, and a real mutation plan/review/apply cycle -- with zero source-code change to DesktopService, RepositorySession, RepositoryTopology, or the mutation engine's repository-model assumptions (only the acquisition adapter is new).

Explicit export/share-back is implemented for both SAF-directory-imported and archive-imported workspaces: a user-invoked action writes the current app-private workspace state back out through SAF (directory write-back or a newly produced archive via a user-selected SAF destination), never automatically or in the background, with obvious-divergence detection attempted where feasible before overwrite (per Decision 0056's write-back model).

The mobile command surface exposes only typed operations (import repository, export workspace, and stubs/no-ops for the Stage-2-reserved clone/pull/push) -- never an arbitrary read/write URI, arbitrary filesystem path, or generic shell -- preserving Decision 0041's typed-command authority boundary; progress/cancellation/error reporting for import and export are typed, not raw strings.

Real Android runtime evidence (on-device, not merely compiled) proves: SAF directory import, SAF/archive import, Workbench operation against the resulting workspace, mutation apply, and export/share-back all function correctly on a real device or emulator, and the Android permission/capability manifest is re-audited to confirm no broad storage, shell, or generic filesystem capability was introduced.

A future embedded-Git seam is established (at minimum, the acquisition-kind/workspace-identity model and command-surface shape accommodate a future clone/pull/push addition without a breaking redesign) but embedded Git itself (git2-rs/gix integration, real clone/fetch/push, remote credentials) is explicitly out of scope for this work item and is deferred to a further follow-up work item created or activated at this item's own closeout if still warranted.
